chapter.title: Paper and Paperboard; Articles of Paper Pulp, of Paper or of Paperboard

page.h1: HTS Chapter 48: Paper and Paperboard; Articles of Paper Pulp, of Paper or of Paperboard — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: What Canada, Mexico, China & the EU Charge on U.S. Paper (HTS Ch. 48) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Rates on U.S. kraftliner, boxes, coated board and tissue in Canada, Mexico, the EU, China, Japan, Costa Rica, Guatemala and the UK, with Canada's 50% surtax.
keywords: tariff on us paper products canada

intro: Six of the eight largest markets charge nothing on most U.S. paper: Mexico, Costa Rica and Guatemala under trade agreements, and the EU, the UK and Japan, whose normal tariff on all paper is zero. **Canada**, the largest buyer, also charges 0% duty, but since September 8, 2026 it adds a **50%** surtax on U.S. corrugated boxes, paper bags, tissue parent rolls and some coated boards and **25%** on toilet paper, tissues and towels. **China** adds 10% to its 2–7.5% rates, and its older counter-tariffs and a 14.9% anti-dumping duty on sack kraft can apply on top. None of these markets requires a product approval for paper itself; the change to plan for is in the EU, where deforestation due-diligence statements are required for paper from December 30, 2026.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada is the largest market ($5.56B, down 6.2%) and the only one with a new tariff on U.S. paper. Since September 8, 2026 corrugated boxes and paper bags (part of 4819, $933M), several coated boards (4810, $578M) and tissue products (4818, $611M) pay a 25% or 50% surtax even under CUSMA, while kraftliner, fluting, folding cartons and plastic-coated paper stay free. Buyers that use the goods in manufacturing or to package food or drink can claim the surtax back.
profile.mainProducts: Boxes, cartons, bags & paper packaging (4819) · Paper coated with plastics, wax or adhesive; thermal & gift wrap (4811)
profile.tariffNow: Free (CUSMA) + 25% or 50% surtax on 17 paper lines

regulator.name: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
regulator.requirement: Paper needs no import permit. CBSA collects the surtax on U.S.-origin goods at entry; the Canadian importer claims remission, for example for goods used in manufacturing or food and beverage packaging, within two years of import

profile.headline: Mexico ($4.00B, down 6.2%) is the largest buyer of U.S. boxes and cartons (4819, $1.03B) and kraftliner (4804, $769M), and charges nothing on paper that meets the USMCA rule of origin. Keep the certification of origin in order: since January 1, 2026 non-qualifying boxes, coated board and uncoated printing paper pay 25–35%.

profile.headline: The EU ($939M, down 3.3%; Italy, Germany, Spain, the Netherlands and Belgium buy most) charges 0% on all paper and buys mainly kraftliner (4804, $253M) and coated board (4810, $238M). What changes is compliance: from December 30, 2026 EU importers must file deforestation due-diligence statements for paper. The U.S. is rated low-risk, so simplified due diligence applies.
profile.mainProducts: Uncoated kraft paper & paperboard (kraftliner, sack kraft) (4804) · Coated paper & paperboard (clay-coated) (4810)

regulator.name: European Commission (EU Deforestation Regulation 2023/1115)
regulator.requirement: From December 30, 2026 (June 30, 2027 for micro and small firms) the EU importer must file a due-diligence statement that the wood fibre was harvested legally and without deforestation or forest degradation after December 31, 2020, with the geolocation of the harvest plots; products made from recovered paper and packaging used only to carry another product are outside the scope

biggestLanes.rate: Free (CUSMA) + 50% on corrugated boxes and bags; folding cartons free
Free (CUSMA) + 25% (toilet paper, tissues, towels) or 50% (napkins, other)

assumptions: Each cell uses one representative six-digit subheading per heading: the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports (for example 4804.11 kraftliner, 4819.10 corrugated boxes, 4811.51 plastic-coated paper, 4810.39 coated kraft board). MFN rates are World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) rates for 2023, the latest year WITS holds; national 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Japan, the EU, the UK and Canada charge 0% MFN on every six-digit line of Chapter 48 (WITS 2023; Canada's 2026 Customs Tariff and Japan's April 2026 schedule show the same), so a trade agreement changes nothing there.

Mexico (USMCA), Costa Rica and Guatemala (CAFTA-DR) apply 0% only to goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate a non-qualifying U.S. good would pay, including Mexico's decree of December 29, 2025 (in force January 1, 2026) where it raised a line under the heading.

Canada's cells name the tariff items in the United States Surtax Order (2026), SOR/2026-186: Schedule 3 (50%) and Schedule 2 (25%). The surtax applies to goods of U.S. origin under the CUSMA marking rules; relief under the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025), such as for inputs to Canadian manufacturing or food and beverage packaging, is not netted out.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to the MFN rate. China's 2018–2019 counter-tariffs (Tariff Commission Announcement 2019 No. 3, and the August 2019 list of Announcement 2019 No. 4, halved to 5% from February 14, 2020 by Announcement 2020 No. 1) are named in each basis but not added, because importers can hold exclusions valid until December 31, 2026. The 14.9% anti-dumping duty applies only to unbleached sack kraft.
VAT and other internal taxes, the cost of EU deforestation due diligence and any trade-remedy duty other than China's sack kraft duty are not included.
